featured_videos.editorial_title: The Best Carnivore Pizza I've Ever Made
featured_videos.commentary: Here's the thing that gets me about this video: the community's already running with it. Cream cheese crusts, waffle iron hacks, Italian sausage variations, spiced-up bases. People aren't just copying the recipe, they're building on it, which is how you know you've actually solved a real problem. Ground chicken pizza hits different because it's not a workaround or a compromise. It's genuinely good food that happens to be zero-carb, and that's what matters most when you're trying to make carnivore sustainable long-term. If you're tired of the same rotations, this one deserves a spot in your meal plan.

featured_videos.title: Carnivores Are Becoming ALLERGIC to Meat
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivores Are Becoming ALLERGIC to Meat
featured_videos.commentary: This one's wild because the comments are split between real alpha-gal stories and the conspiracy rabbit hole, but the actual experiences hit different. People are describing years of confusion, failed doctor visits, and then finding their way back to meat through acupuncture or extended fasting. That's the story that matters here, not the Bill Gates narrative. If you've been following carnivore long enough, you know alpha-gal is real, it's tick-borne, and it's worth being aware of if you're in high-risk areas. The good news buried in these comments is that some people have reversed it, which gives real hope to anyone dealing with this.

featured_videos.title: I Only Eat THESE 3 Meals On Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Only Eat THESE 3 Meals On Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: One thing I've noticed coaching people through carnivore is that simplicity wins every single time. Kerry's approach here is exactly what works in the real world, not what sounds impressive on Instagram. The comment about that kid knowing the difference between fresh and store eggs says everything, right? Kids taste truth. And honestly, when someone's 1200+ days deep and still eating the same three meals, that's not boring, that's freedom from decision fatigue and food noise. The "beef fudge" comment made me smile because that's the kind of thing people discover after they stop overthinking macros and just eat what their body actually wants.

featured_videos.title: 3 EASY Meals I’ve Eaten for 3 Years on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Emmathecarnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 EASY Meals I’ve Eaten for 3 Years on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Three years on the same three meals and still thriving. that's the opposite of what most diet culture tells you. The comments nailed it: people get carnivore fatigue and then forget how boring-simple it actually works. Emma's showing exactly what sustainability looks like. No reinventing the wheel every Monday, no "new protocol," just eggs, bacon, and ground beef done well. That's the real win.

featured_videos.title: What I eat for carnivore weight loss
featured_videos.creator: Courtney Luna
featured_videos.editorial_title: What I eat for carnivore weight loss
featured_videos.commentary: The comments section here is basically a masterclass in what actually works for fat loss on carnivore, and it's not complicated. Ground beef, meatballs, burger patties, crispy everything, sardines, hot dogs, eggs. Nobody's overthinking macros or talking about "optimal meal timing". they're just eating meat they enjoy and getting results. What strikes me most is how many people mention simplicity as their secret weapon, and that tracks with what I've seen coaching. When your food list gets short, your decision fatigue drops, your compliance goes up, and weight loss follows. The variety here matters too though. Someone doing OMAD one day, 2MAD the next, and full meals on the third is basically metabolic cycling without the stress of rigid protocols. That's the real win.
